A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SpeeD. All 21 pages of v1 and 24 pages of v2, including appendices A–D, support comparison. Text, equations, tables and rendered figures are readable and can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original diffusion-training comparisons, component ablations, robustness evaluations and generated images in Section 3 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds longer-training comparisons and sensitivity experiments in Appendix B.1.

M1.justification: The asymmetric sampling rule, threshold selection and change-aware weighting remain unchanged. New Section 2.3 generalizes the mathematical discussion beyond DDPM but does not specify a changed SpeeD procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MetFaces, FFHQ, ImageNet-1K, CIFAR-10 and MS-COCO, covering unconditional, class-conditional, text-to-image and super-resolution generation. The added experiments vary training duration, guidance and model configurations within this coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 10 adds ANT-UW and TskDif-Cur, as labeled and cited there, to the FFHQ comparisons. The original DiT, P2, Min-SNR, Log-Normal and CLTS comparisons and the MDT/FDM compatibility comparisons remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds 100K-iteration FFHQ evaluations, guidance scales from 0.75 to 3, and DiT-S/2, B/2 and XL/2 size comparisons. Its training-recipe table changes FFHQ from 50K to 100K iterations, while the retained main comparison still specifies 50K; this does not establish that the original results were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix B.1 adds guidance-scale sensitivity tests on MS-COCO and CIFAR-10 and a DiT-size ablation on FFHQ. These extend the existing robustness evidence; the original component, suppression-intensity and weighting-ceiling ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for the experiments. The theoretical noise variances are not experimental uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v2 substantially expands results on sustained training, additional comparator rankings and guidance/model-size sensitivity in Tables 10–13. For example, the new 100K linear-schedule FFHQ comparison reports 5.8 for SpeeD, 7.8 for DiT-XL/2, 6.3 for ANT-UW and 6.7 for TskDif-Cur. Original results remain unchanged; these are additional settings, not revised same-setting performance.

T1.justification: New Section 2.3 introduces an s–sigma SDE formulation, generalized process-increment distributions and derivative expressions. New Table 1 specializes the discussion to VP, VE and EDM schedules, substantially extending the formal scope beyond the retained DDPM theorem and appendix proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and principal conclusion retain the same claims: suppress redundant convergence-area sampling, emphasize rapidly changing increments, and achieve approximately threefold training acceleration with broad architectural compatibility. Added evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Section 2.3 adds arguments favoring noise-scale-based design and reduced sampling of low-SNR increments. v2 removes v1's limitations/future-work paragraph identifying video generation and consistency models as future extensions, while Appendix A.1 newly argues that ultimate-convergence comparisons are unnecessary for the paper's acceleration objective.

D1.justification: The supplied code destination changes from 1zeryu/SpeeD to NUS-HPC-AI-Lab/SpeeD. v2 also updates the FFHQ training recipe and documents configurations for the added experiments. Existing optimizer, architecture, preprocessing and hardware disclosures largely remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references on negative transfer, task routing/curricula, timestep sampling and training bias, plus the SDE reference supporting Section 2.3. Section 4 briefly incorporates the multitask-learning perspective and additional compatibility positioning; the broader related-work narrative remains.

P1.justification: v2 moves visualization from Section 3.6 to 3.1, reframes DDPM as a case study, introduces appendix subsections and makes localized prose edits. Author text and citation style also change, but most existing prose and the overall narrative are retained.

P2.justification: v2 retypesets the document with different title, heading, header and bibliography formatting, adds the schedule table and four experimental tables, and relocates several displays. The original visualization becomes Figure 4 and appendix galleries are regrouped; existing plots and generated-image examples themselves are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added longer-training comparisons, additional baselines and sensitivity tests strengthen empirical support. However, the new theoretical generalization contains internal inconsistencies: Table 1 lists EDM sigma^2=t^2 but d sigma/dt=2t, with a similar inconsistency for VE. Together with conflicting FFHQ budget descriptions and removal of explicit limitations, these weaken the revision's reliability and qualification of its claims. The benefits and harms do not support a clear net quality judgment.
